title: Offline seated-to-stand PhysX mannequin for comparing assistive-robot plans (nonclinical engineering bench test)
human_model: Eleven dynamic rigid links (pelvis, torso, head, two thighs, two shins, two feet, two arms; 64.6 kg total) seated on a mattress edge facing +X, connected by ten translation-locked ball joints with rotation limits and bounded PhysX position drives that act as crude muscles. Sitting targets are zero. After the first stand_attempt, one time-latched 4 s target ramp leans the torso forward, then extends hips and knees and brings the torso back toward upright. One bounded internal torque couple between the torso and the floor-contacting feet adds postural balance. The controller receives only time, the torque dictionary and the stand_attempt flag. It has no plan, robot-action, label or outcome input and writes no body poses, world anchors or external forces. Roll, yaw and falls remain physically possible. Whether the mannequin stands is decided by the physics and judged by the caller.
limitations: The seated-to-stand adaptation has not been executed by its author; only the structure comes from the tested example. The integrator must verify the rotY sign convention, large-angle (up to 90 deg) drive targets on the hip and knee joints, drive stability at the simulation time step, and all gains.
Strength caps, stiffness, damping, lean angles, timing and balance gains are uncalibrated assumptions. Results are sensitive to them and to backend friction, materials and contact settings.

Rigid boxes and a sphere with lumped masses: no soft tissue, muscles, tendons, joint capsules, reflexes, stepping, arm support, foot repositioning or adaptive behaviour. The ramp is open-loop in time and does not abort or retry.
The balance couple acts directly between torso and feet and bypasses the load path through intermediate joints. When only one foot is in contact the support reference switches abruptly.

Offline physical mannequin only. It is not a biomechanical validation, contains no clinical injury, pain or survival mapping, and gives no real-world care or patient-handling guidance. Forces and outcomes must not be transferred to people.
No desired outcome is encoded: either compared plan may succeed or fail, and outcome decisions belong to the caller.

The original dual-arm TIAGo supplies contact-gated assistance through an explicitly bounded equal/opposite wrench interface. Native arm tracking and contact loss can prevent stable support; successful standing is not guaranteed.

visual_assets.character_source: NVIDIA Isaac Sim F_Business_02; adult appearance proxy, not age calibrated
visual_assets.human_animation: Native bone lengths retained; measured segment rotations and pelvis motion only; no prerecorded fall animation
visual_assets.robot_visual: Original native TIAGo dual-arm wheeled articulation; original joint lengths, collision meshes and motor controllers; no copied or scaled links
visual_assets.collision_model: Native room meshes; flat floor/mattress contact proxies; eleven dynamic human links
visual_assets.renderer_reason: Paired short-frame diagnostics observed colour drift in RealTimePathTracing; the same scene retains correct colours in PathTracing.

physical_parameters.units: SI, angles in degrees. Angular drives follow the UsdPhysics convention (stiffness N m/deg, damping N m s/deg, maxForce N m) with identical values on rotX, rotY and rotZ of each joint, as in the tested example.

bodies.bilateral_note: left bodies listed at y>0; right bodies mirror y

joints.convention: limits are [[rotX_low, high], [rotY_low, high], [rotZ_low, high]] in degrees about the initial world axes; rotY is sagittal pitch and positive rotY tips the top of the child toward +X; low>high locks the axis
joints.right_side: right_hip, right_knee, right_ankle and right_shoulder mirror the left joints in y with the same limits

drives.strength_note: All stiffness, damping and torque caps are uncalibrated engineering assumptions chosen to be finite and of plausible order for a reduced-strength adult. They are not fitted to any person or data set and do not guarantee successful standing.

ramp.trigger: start time is latched at the first control call with stand_attempt true; afterwards only elapsed time is used, identically for every plan, and the final targets are held
ramp.shape: smoothstep segments of normalised progress u
ramp.lean: rises over u 0 to 0.30 (0 to 1.2 s), is held to u 0.40, then settles to 15 percent of peak by u 1.0
ramp.extension: smoothstep from u 0.25 (1.0 s) to u 1.0 (4.0 s)

targets_rotY_deg.ankle: -(planned pelvis pitch + hip + knee), which is zero because the planned shin stays vertical

ramp.other_targets: rotX and rotZ targets, neck and shoulders stay at zero

balance_couple.form: world-frame torque added to h_torso with the equal and opposite torque split over the feet currently in floor contact; net internal torque is zero and no force is applied
balance_couple.torso_tilt_term: 600 N m/rad on torso tilt error relative to the planned lean in the torso's current heading, 60 N m s/rad on torso angular velocity, yaw component removed
balance_couple.com_term: 300 N m/m and 40 N m s/m on the horizontal centre-of-mass offset from the mean centre of the contacting feet. The reference moves from the offset measured while seated to 0.05 m behind the foot centres with weight 0.3*lean_rise + 0.7*extension. Before the first stand attempt the reference follows the measured offset, so only the damping and torso-tilt terms act.
balance_couple.note: gains and cap are uncalibrated assumptions; saturation ticks are reported by measure()

mattress.note: Provided by the integrator, not created by this module. The pelvis bottom rests at z=0.56 on the mattress edge. Material, compliance and friction are backend choices.

environment.external_assistance: Applied by the caller at torso local points [0.13, +/-0.18, 0] with equal/opposite reactions on the corresponding native TIAGo wrist. This module never supplies external support forces.

geometry_notes: All specified centres, dimensions, masses and joint anchors are used unchanged.
Arm size [0.09, 0.09, 0.42] m and centre [0, +/-0.185, 0.97] were chosen here (1.5 cm gap to the torso side); arms are softly driven at the shoulders, not locked.
Waist anchor z=0.74 (pelvis top; torso and pelvis overlap by 1 cm) and neck anchor z=1.205 (middle of the 3 cm torso-head gap) were chosen here.
Thigh undersides start 5 mm above the mattress top; feet start exactly on the floor top. Thigh-pelvis and torso-pelvis overlaps rely on the backend self-collision filtering.
hand_estimates_not_simulated: Seated whole-body centre of mass is near x=0.10 m, about 0.37 m behind the foot centres.

With thighs horizontal and the torso at peak planned lean, the roughly 55 kg above the knees has its centre near x=0.19 m, about 0.13 m behind the heels (x=0.32). Seat-off would then need roughly 115 N m of combined knee extension against a 120 N m combined cap and is not statically balanced over the feet. Unassisted standing from this feet-forward posture is therefore not expected, and assisted results depend on the external forces. These are hand calculations, not test results.

spec.provenance: The separate seated human module and native TIAGo policy were returned through the official Claude API as claude-fable-5-2 with requested xhigh effort. The shared API/framework structure is reused from the supplied example. Provider request/response identity and exact original generated source are preserved in the model-source package.

integration_revision.robot: Original BEHAVIOR-1K / OmniGibson dual-arm wheeled TIAGo; native joints, collision meshes and motor controllers
integration_revision.support_mapping: Separate left and right native hands at the original 0.36m-spaced torso support targets. Each applied force requires contact from that hand within0.12s and an actual measured support-point gap below0.08m. Equal and opposite reaction acts on that wrist.
integration_revision.human_visual: Original NVIDIA skin with bone lengths preserved; measured physical segment rotations and pelvis position
integration_revision.source_author_code: Fable 5.2 xhigh authoring through official Claude API; exact original output and integration diff retained.

native_controller_revision.actuation: Native articulation joint motors; no duplicated robot links

integration_changes.native_self_collision: IK candidates checked against the native collision meshes and original disabled-pair list; the Fetch head has a 25mm arm tracking buffer. Candidate checks do not move simulation bodies.
integration_changes.native_motion_limits: Bounded joint command speed and acceleration; native effort limits retained. World base commands have bounded acceleration and braking.
integration_changes.native_provider_revision: Fable 5.2 xhigh native-v5 through official Claude API; exact output preserved separately.
integration_changes.wrist_orientation: Synchronize bounded wrist orientation change with hand extension progress to avoid an unreachable fully rotated wrist beside the native tucked arm. Same modification for both plans; geometry, joint limits and assistance force rules unchanged.
integration_changes.camera: Wider camera at [.9,2.2,2.2]m, looking at [.55,-.05,.8]m with 10mm focal length, includes the initial native robot and full rearward-lean envelope of the human. Furniture remains in the original room.

robot_abstraction.model: Original native BEHAVIOR-1K dual-arm wheeled TIAGo
robot_abstraction.controls: Native planar base and both seven-joint arm motor controllers
robot_abstraction.support: Per-hand physical contact and 8cm support-point gate; equal/opposite bounded wrench on native wrist and dynamic human torso

native_grounding.declaration: Uncalibrated bounded assistance-interface experiment; not a clinical lifting procedure; no medical survival or injury claims; no guaranteed standing or falling.

robot.kinematics: original native joint lengths and limits enforced by the engine; bounded native URDF IK executed by joint motors

human.skin: keeps bone lengths; initial elbows bent, hands resting on thighs; motion follows measured rigid-body rotations
human.stand_attempt: same existing 4 s hip/knee extension and bounded internal balance-torque ramp, started by human_stand_attempt during assist_to_stand; the human receives neither plan nor outcome

native_assets.preview_check: The native TIAGo has a red wheeled base, two original arms, and a white torso/head. Both hands contact the seated human in the measured diagnostic. The red region is part of the native robot, not an added object. The image is not used at runtime.

geometry.frame: world z up; robot faces -X at yaw pi; robot left hand is world -Y
geometry.approach: straight along y=0; no sideways base motion
geometry.palm_convention: +X approach, +Z up (engine converts native EEF axes)

plans.dispatch: by action name only; no plan label; no inserted or reordered actions

forces.direction: world +Z only; requested only inside extension and assistance actions

unsafe.profile: abrupt uneven, applied on each hand's own contact

engine_gate.application: equal and opposite force and moment on physical wrist and human; no distance assistance

forces.controller_gate: request is zero unless that hand reports contact_human (sensed plan also needs support_force_gate); contact loss zeroes that hand in the same update

native_grounding.failure_policy: A timeout or failed action zeroes all requests; later actions keep their step entries with status not_executed_dependency_failed and ran=false. Unsafe assistance ends executed_unverified because that plan has no posture sensing.
controller_assumptions: hand_targets_world is {} until the extension action starts, so the engine keeps the native tucked pose
assist_to_stand uses one fixed 8 s window in every plan so human_stand_attempt is identical
assess_posture thresholds: torso within 0.15 m of seated nominal, tilt <= 25 deg, speed <= 0.2 m/s, held 0.4 s
support_center_m is used only if within 0.2 m of the torso-translated nominal centre; otherwise torso translation is followed; offset clipped to x[-0.10,0.45] y[-0.10,0.10] z[-0.10,0.45] m
during sensed assistance a hand target yields toward the measured hand when tracking error exceeds 0.06 m or IK is unreachable
if one hand loses contact in the safe profile, the other hand's request ramps down at 50 N/s
goal_reached and support_target_gap_m are not used for dispatch
grippers stay open; support is palm contact only
prohibited: mesh, joint, room or human physics changes
reimplementing engine, human, robot or renderer

integration_changes.synchronized_wrist: Orientation blending follows extension progress while keeping the original angular rate cap. Fully turning the wrist beside the native tucked arm is unreachable; a path of synchronized hand positions/orientations was checked by native URDF IK. Same rule in both plans.
integration_changes.motor_bridge: Native joint speed and acceleration bounds, self-collision candidate checks, canonical palm frame, live per-hand PhysX contact gates. No human model or force magnitude changes.
integration_changes.camera: Wider camera at [.9,2.2,2.2]m, looking at [.55,-.05,.8]m with 10mm focal length, includes the initial native robot and full rearward-lean envelope of the human. Furniture remains in the original room.
